item.title: The Story of James Weldon Johnson, Creator of the Black National Anthem
item.description: On February 12, 1900, five hundred students of the segregated Stanton School in Jacksonville, Florida, where James Weldon Johnson was the principal, celebrated President Abraham Lincoln’s birthday by giving the first-ever performance of “Lift Every Voice and Sing,” the song that has since became known as the Black National Anthem.
